note: tac_lite is a node_access GRANTS module: it grants view/update/delete on nodes based on the taxonomy terms they carry (hook_node_access_records + hook_node_grants), realm tac_lite_scheme_<n>. All configuration lives in ONE config object, tac_lite.settings (tac_lite_categories = vocab ids, tac_lite_schemes = count 1-7, tac_lite_storage_type = tid|uuid, tac_lite_config_scheme_<n> = {name, perms[grant_view/grant_update/grant_delete], unpublished, term_visibility, tac_lite_create}, tac_lite_grants_scheme_<n> = role defaults); per-user grants are in user.data. There is no tac_lite.scheme.N object. Because this is a node-access module, ALL eval cases are deliberately grounded in tac_lite.settings config only and leave tac_lite_categories null, so hook_node_access_records emits NO grants and no node_access rebuild is needed and no grants are left broken. Baseline: tac_lite_categories null, tac_lite_schemes 1, no scheme config, storage defaults to tid.

evals.prompt: How does the Drupal module tac_lite (Taxonomy Access Control Lite) actually control who can see a node, and which node operations can it affect? Does it grant or revoke access?
evals.expected_output: It uses Drupal's node_access grants system: hook_node_access_records writes grant rows (gid = term id) per scheme realm for a node's tac_lite terms, and hook_node_grants returns the terms a user may access. It can grant view, update and delete. It only GRANTS access (reveals content) — it cannot hide content the user already may see.

evals.prompt: In tac_lite, which config object stores its settings and what are the main keys for choosing the controlled vocabularies and the number of schemes? Where is the admin page?
evals.expected_output: Everything lives in the tac_lite.settings config object: tac_lite_categories (vocabulary ids), tac_lite_schemes (number of schemes, up to 7), tac_lite_storage_type (tid|uuid), and tac_lite_config_scheme_<n> / tac_lite_grants_scheme_<n>. Admin UI at /admin/config/people/tac_lite (route tac_lite.administration).

evals.prompt: Using tac_lite, how do you give one specific user access to content in a category, and what must you do after configuring or changing a scheme?
evals.expected_output: Grant a single user terms on the 'Access by taxonomy' tab of their account edit page (/user/{user}/tac_lite, stored via user.data). After changing schemes you must rebuild node access permissions (Reports -> Status report -> Rebuild permissions, or node_access_rebuild()).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, tac_lite scheme 1 has been configured. Inspect the live tac_lite configuration and tell me the scheme's name and which node permission(s) it grants.
evals.expected_output: Scheme 1 is named 'Read access' and grants node view: tac_lite.settings tac_lite_config_scheme_1 has name 'Read access' and perms including grant_view. Discoverable via drush cget tac_lite.settings tac_lite_config_scheme_1.

evals.prompt: On this site, how does tac_lite identify the taxonomy terms in its access grants — by term id (tid) or by uuid? Inspect the live tac_lite settings and answer.
evals.expected_output: By uuid: tac_lite.settings tac_lite_storage_type is 'uuid' (the code reads tac_lite_storage_type, defaulting to tid when unset). Discoverable via drush cget tac_lite.settings tac_lite_storage_type.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure tac_lite scheme 1 so that it grants node 'view' access (add the view permission to the scheme). Apply the change to the live tac_lite configuration. (You do not need to select a vocabulary or rebuild node access for this task.)
evals.expected_output: tac_lite.settings tac_lite_config_scheme_1.perms includes grant_view (set via the scheme tab's Permissions multiselect, or by editing the config: perms => ['grant_view']).

evals.prompt: On this site tac_lite is currently set up with a single access scheme. Increase the number of tac_lite schemes to 2 and apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: tac_lite.settings tac_lite_schemes is set to 2 (via the number-of-schemes setting on /admin/config/people/tac_lite, or by editing the config value).
